standard_prerequisites.name: Galois cohomology of a torus split by a finite Galois covering, via the Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used inside the counted proof at lines 578-591

standard_prerequisites.name: Finiteness of the ideal class group and Dirichlet's unit theorem over a global field
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes H^0(V, G) of finite type and H^1(V, G) of finite type (finite when U is not X).

standard_prerequisites.name: Artin-Mazur-Milne duality for fppf cohomology
standard_prerequisites.use: Transfers the finiteness of H^1(U, N) to H^2_c(U, N^D).

core_obligations: Part 1, H^0 and H^1 of a torus: choose a finite connected etale Galois covering V of U splitting T, use that T(V) is isomorphic to H^0(V, G)^r and Dirichlet's theorem to get H^0(U, T) of finite type, then run the Hochschild-Serre exact sequence and the finiteness of the ideal class group to bound H^1(U, T) (proof lines 578-599).

Part 2, finite group schemes of multiplicative type: reduce to U different from X, use that a finitely generated Galois module of multiplicative type is a quotient of a torsion-free one to embed N into an exact sequence 0 -> N -> T_1 -> T_2 -> 0 of U-tori, and split the resulting cohomology sequence (proof lines 601-616).

Part 2, conclusion: H^1(U, T_1) is finite by part 1, and the map H^0(U, T_2) -> H^1(U, N) factorises through H^0(U, T_2)/n with n the order of N, which is finite because H^0(U, T_2) is of finite type; then H^2_c(U, N^D) is finite by Artin-Mazur-Milne duality (proof lines 617-623).
proof_roadmap: Split the torus along a finite Galois covering and read off finite generation of H^0 and H^1 from Dirichlet's theorem, the class group and Hochschild-Serre (proof lines 578-599).
Embed the multiplicative-type group scheme into a two-term sequence of tori and control the connecting map by dividing out by the order of N (proof lines 601-621).
Apply Artin-Mazur-Milne duality for the H^2_c finiteness (proof lines 622-623).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is about a curve U over a global field of positive characteristic: it claims that for a torus T the groups H^0(U, T) and H^1(U, T) are of finite type (finite when U is not X), and that for a finite group scheme N of multiplicative type both H^1(U, N) and H^2_c(U, N^D) are finite (statement lines 561-573). The proof splits T along a finite connected etale Galois covering, uses Dirichlet's theorem and the finiteness of the ideal class group to bound the two cohomology groups, and then embeds N into a sequence of two tori so that the finiteness reduces to an image computation plus a division by the order of N (proof lines 578-621). The step that is not a routine citation is the second one: the connecting map H^0(U, T_2) -> H^1(U, N) has to be controlled by factoring it through H^0(U, T_2)/n, and the author supplies that factorisation explicitly rather than invoking a general finiteness principle. The duality input at the end is a cited theorem, so the card is H2.
